updates.title: Documentation, and a change in approach
updates.summary: Before any code was written, we wrote up the project proposal, scope, roadmap and a research plan — then decided to change how we'd actually work.
completed: Wrote the project proposal: overview, context, stakeholders, and the initial areas to investigate.
Drafted the project roadmap and revised its effort/duration estimate (2 students, 5 hours/week each, 16 weeks).
Wrote a research plan for Weeks 3–6 covering who we'd talk to, what we wanted to learn, and when.
updates.approachChange: The original roadmap laid out fixed phases — research, then define and design, then a single test-and-improve phase near the end. We decided against that: instead we're working in short cycles, building a prototype, showing it to real users, gathering feedback, improving it, and repeating. Research and user conversations now happen alongside each cycle instead of as one separate phase.
nextSteps: Start the first build-show-learn cycle instead of the original Week 3–6 research phase.

updates.title: First prototype: real project data, live and shared
updates.summary: Following the change in approach above, this is the first build-show-learn cycle: a working prototype of the project directory, now loaded with the batch's real projects and mentors, deployed live, and shared with the coordinator for feedback.
completed: Designed the data model and screens for a project directory, grouped into batches, with role-based permissions for students, mentors and the coordinator.
Loaded the real PDM 2025–2027 batch roster and all 22 registered project ideas from the batch's project registration form, replacing the placeholder demo data the prototype started with.

Sent the programme coordinator a status update covering this prototype, the live link, the GitHub repo and this progress page, with two open questions: what details a final year project record actually needs, and who should be responsible for entering them (coordinator vs. mentor).
added: Project directory home page: browse as cards or a table, search by title, and filter by batch, domain, status, or "only mine".
Batches: list view, a side-panel to create a new batch, and a batch detail page grouping its projects.
Add Project flow (side panel) and full project form: title, description, domain, team members, mentor, problem, outcome, and material links.
Role switcher (student / mentor / coordinator) that demonstrates what each role can see and do, ahead of real sign-in.
Duplicate-title detection that flags likely repeat project titles before saving.
This Project progress page and a sidebar collaborators panel.
A Mentor filter in the project directory, so a coordinator can shortlist projects by who mentors them.
A three-dot actions menu on project and batch cards: Edit, Share (copies a link), and Archive/Restore.
An Edit batch panel, so a batch's years, name and description can be changed after it's created.
The live prototype is now deployed and connected to GitHub, so every push updates it automatically: https://pdm-project-manager.vercel.app
improved: When a mentor creates a project, the Mentor field is now pre-filled with their own name and locked, since a mentor always mentors the projects they add.
Add Project and Add Batch panels keep Cancel/Save pinned in a fixed footer instead of scrolling away with the form.
The top header bar is now sticky so it stays visible while a page scrolls.
The sidebar's selected item now shows solid white in light mode for clearer contrast; dark mode is unchanged.

Project cards now show the team and mentor as avatars (initials for now, real photos later) instead of a plain name list, and the directory grid is capped at two columns with a single-line title so cards stay easy to scan.
Archiving a batch is blocked while it still has active projects in it, so a batch can't accidentally hide its own projects.
removed: The cover-image / placeholder graphic on project cards in the directory — cards now lead with status, title, team, and mentor.
The batch name shown on every project card in its own directory — redundant once you're already inside that batch.
The Ongoing/Completed status filter and the three placeholder batches (2022–24, 2023–25, 2024–26) — trimmed for now to keep the directory to the one real batch.
unfinished: Not shown to real users yet — no testing or feedback has been recorded for this prototype.
Waiting on the coordinator's answer on what fields a project record actually needs and who should own entering them — real project data was loaded as-is without guessing at either.
nextSteps: Show this prototype to students, mentors and/or the coordinator and record what we learn.
No persistence yet — data resets on refresh; a real backend/database is next.
No real authentication yet; the role switcher stands in for sign-in.
"Materials" are pasted links today, not uploaded files.

updates.title: Every must-have feature built, and the design system rebuilt twice to get it right
updates.summary: This period turned the project directory into the full lifecycle system the feature plan promised — all forty must-have features are in the running app, verified with a scripted two-tab test. The interface direction was tried twice along the way: a bold display-type redesign was rejected at review as unprofessional for this tool's real audience, so it was rebuilt a second time into a refined, warm-neutral academic system, documented live at /design-system. The Directory (batches, rosters, the project register) came back after the redesign had folded it away, and a run of consistency fixes closed out the period.
completed: Wrote the 28-week workflow map (docs/01-workflow-map.md): phases, per-stakeholder loops, a friction register (F1–F29), known-vs-must-validate assumptions, a scan of about 40 comparable tools, and the public IIITH graduation-projects archive.

Wrote the MoSCoW feature catalogue (docs/02-feature-catalogue-moscow.md): 162 features across 17 modules, each traced to the friction it removes — 40 Must, 57 Should, 46 Could, 17 Delighter, 2 explicit Won't.

Turned both into submission-ready Word documents (PDM-Workflow-Report.docx, PDM-Feature-Plan.docx) for faculty review, with the process drawn as diagrams and a build pipeline that renders real page numbers.

Verified the full feature build with a scripted two-tab run covering submit, review, return-with-reason, and the permission boundary, plus a browser smoke test across every screen and overlay as all three roles.
added: All forty must-have features from the catalogue, built into the app: a real milestone lifecycle (12 checkpoints per team, not-started through accepted), turn-in/review/accept-or-return with a required reason, meetings with minutes and owned actions, announcements with a live audience count, and a 22×12 grid built as an accessible ARIA grid rather than a table.
A live, documented design system at /design-system — now with a full component gallery showing every UI primitive the app actually imports, plus a note of what's still unused.
npm run contrast: recomputes all 42 colour-contrast rules from the token file and fails the build if one drifts.
npm run smoke: drives a real browser through every screen and every overlay as all three roles.
The Directory restored as its own page: a batch index, then a batch's roster and its project register (title, domain, team, mentor, status), searchable and filterable.
Project progress (this page) reconnected to the sidebar — it existed with real content but had no link anywhere in the app since the redesign.
improved: Navigation restructured to the same words for every role — Today, Projects, Checkpoints, Messages, Directory, Updates — with the coordinator's Programme group beneath, read from one file so the sidebar and the command palette can't drift apart.

Colour, radius and motion rebuilt around a warm neutral ground with one indigo accent: radius graduated by role instead of one value everywhere, and three easing curves reconciled against real accessibility numbers.

Form fields — Select, Textarea, Checkbox, RadioGroup, and the command-palette search box — brought to the same plain white/bordered look as a text input, instead of a heavier grey fill that made them read as a different, inconsistent design.

The batch/project register given room to breathe: Students split into its own tab instead of stacking under Projects, table rows size to their content instead of truncating long titles, and a status badge that was misusing the one-accent-per-screen colour was toned down to a muted variant.
fixed: Two overlay crashes (the account menu, the command palette) caused by assuming a component's API instead of reading it — both are now covered by the smoke test.
Contrast failures found while rebuilding the system: an invisible "not started" status glyph, input borders under the WCAG boundary minimum, and white text on the dark-mode accent.
A mentor-allocation warning that flagged a real mentor's ten teams as a data conflict, when the number was simply correct — removed rather than changing the data to fit the check.
removed: The display-type redesign tried mid-period (Bricolage Grotesque, a lime accent, 2–3px radius) — reverted after review as unprofessional for professors and external faculty looking at one projected screen.
blockers: Still no coordinator confirmation on the two open questions from the last update: what fields a project record actually needs, and who should own entering them.
The mentor allocation is still the batch's registration-form data, unconfirmed against the coordinator's real mentoring lines — the roster stays a draft, not a record, until that's settled.
unfinished: Nothing was shown to students or mentors this period; no new testing or feedback was recorded.
No real authentication or persistence yet — the role switcher and a store that resets on refresh still stand in for both.
updates.approachChange: The interface was rebuilt twice this period. The first pass chose a bold display-type direction — Bricolage Grotesque, a lime accent, radii dropped to 2–3px — to make the tool look distinct. It was rejected at review as unprofessional for the audience this tool is actually for: professors and external faculty, often looking at one projected screen in a supervision meeting. Rather than patch it, the system was rebuilt a second time around a warm-neutral, indigo-accented, contrast-checked system — the one live now at /design-system.
nextSteps: Get the coordinator's answer on the two open questions, and get the mentor allocation numbers confirmed.
Show the rebuilt interface and the restored Directory to students and mentors, and record what's learned.
Real authentication and a real database are still next — the role switcher and the reset-on-refresh store were always meant to be stand-ins.
